about: Shared cases for "is this event hard to undo?" Made by tools/hard-to-undo-vectors.mjs; run by test/hard-to-undo-vectors.test.ts (Keykin) and HardToUndoVectorsTest (Marble). `answers` is what each implementation answers today, with `level` (1: Are you sure?, 2: never by accident; null when nobody is asked); `expect` is the box's decision and `level` its level, since the box is the authority (Marble may ask more on top). `prev` is the last version of that list or profile the signer saw (null: none). `now` is the signer's clock. Events are unsigned; their pubkey is a stand-in.

implementations.box: Keykin box/box.ts #sign with src/destructive.ts judge(event, prev, now). ask, level 1: the box answers needs_tap unless the request says tapped: true. ask, level 2: it answers needs_fingerprint (no_chip_key to a device with no chip key) unless the request carries a valid fp by the asking device's chip key, as for an account change; tapped alone never signs it. refuse: it answers dated_ahead. All carry says as why
implementations.marble: Marble android/signer/src/main/java/cc/aaro/cosign/core/Policy.kt, refuse(e, now) then question(e, prev, now): its own check on top of the box, and its only one with no box in the signature

outcomes.marble: Marble Android with a box. signs: nobody is asked. asks: the phone asks once (in its own words when its rules ask, else in the box's), and Yes signs with tapped. fingerprint: the same question, and Yes goes on to the fingerprint, sent as fp for the box to check (level 2 on either side). refuses: never signed.
outcomes.marbleAlone: Marble Android with no box in the signature (the whole key on the phone, or another device helping while the box is off): its own rules only. asks: Yes or No. fingerprint: Yes, then the phone's fingerprint prompt (none on a phone with no fingerprint set up). refuses: never signed.
outcomes.mac: Marble for the Mac. signs: nobody is asked. asks: the box answers needs_tap, the Mac asks with the box's words, and Yes sends it again with tapped. phone: the box answers needs_fingerprint; the Mac shows the box's words and that this is done from the phone, with no Yes, and sends nothing more. refuses: never signed.
outcomes.keykinDevices: Devices that cannot ask a person (the NIP-46 bunker in src/nip46.ts, the command-line device). needs_tap, needs_fingerprint or dated_ahead: refused, and the error carries the box's words (for needs_fingerprint, also that it is done from the phone). signs: signed.

none of name, display_name, about, picture, nip05, lud16 is filled, whatever came before. One strict reading: the content is exactly one JSON object as Keykin reads kind 0 (src/bytes.ts parseJson, numbers by grammar); a key named twice, a control character in a string, a lone surrogate, a byte order mark, loose JSON or text after it make it no profile, which counts as empty. A field is filled when it is a string with a character that is not white space, a control character or a format character
rules.says: "Wipe your profile: <fields that were filled before>" ("everything" when none were, or there is no earlier version)
